items.title: Welcome to Satyrn Zen
items.text:
The purpose of this site is to:

  • provide learning materials to understand AI Systems, components, and workflows
  • offer materials to help you create and build your ideas with AI tools and local models
  • share Satyrn.ai's work and community projects

This site will contain information created and curated by the Satyrn.ai team. It will also provide a place for third-party community contributions that fit with Satyrn.ai's mission.

items.title: How to run a local coding agent with Ollama in Docker
path: How to run a local coding agent with Ollama in Docker

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Running Ollama from the CLI is the quickest way to chat with a model. If you want a local model that a coding agent can actually drive - reading files, running commands, writing code - run Ollama in Docker and point a coding agent at it.

This guide runs JetBrains Mellum2 in a container and uses Pi as the coding agent.

Why Mellum2?

A coding agent needs the model to emit structured tool calls, which Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint turns into a real tool_calls response. Mellum2 emits tool calls reliably, which makes it usable as an agent on modest hardware.
path: How to run a local coding agent with Ollama in Docker

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
If you are new to Ollama, start with How to run a local model with Ollama.

You need:

  • Docker with Compose, to run Ollama.
  • Pi, the coding agent that talks to the local model.
  • About 16GB of RAM.

Check the model size requirements before picking a tag.
path: How to run a local coding agent with Ollama in Docker

items.title: Start Ollama in Docker
items.text:
1. Create a docker-compose.yaml file in an empty directory.

    services:
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama
    container_name: ollama
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      - ollama_data:/root/.ollama

volumes:
  ollama_data:

    The named ollama_data volume keeps downloaded models between restarts, so you only pull each model once.

  2. Start the container from that directory.

    docker compose up -d

  3. Pull the model into the running container. This is a one-time download.

    docker exec -it ollama ollama pull JetBrains/mellum2-instruct-q4_k_m

  4. Confirm the model is available.

    docker exec -it ollama ollama list

    You should see JetBrains/mellum2-instruct-q4_k_m:latest in the list.

The model is now served on http://localhost:11434, with an OpenAI-compatible API at http://localhost:11434/v1.
path: How to run a local coding agent with Ollama in Docker

items.title: Point Pi at the local model
items.text:
1. Register the local Ollama provider in Pi's global config. This is also a one-time step.

    mkdir -p ~/.pi/agent

    Create ~/.pi/agent/models.json with the following content:

    {
  "providers": {
    "ollama": {
      "baseUrl": "http://localhost:11434/v1",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "apiKey": "ollama",
      "models": [
        {
          "id": "JetBrains/mellum2-instruct-q4_k_m:latest",
          "name": "Mellum2 Instruct q4_k_m (local)"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

    Ollama ignores the apiKey value, but the field must be present because the endpoint is OpenAI-compatible.

  2. Launch Pi from the project directory.

    pi

  3. Give the agent a task, such as "list the files in this directory" or "create a file called hello.py that prints hello".
path: How to run a local coding agent with Ollama in Docker

items.title: Stop and clean up
items.text:
1. Stop the container when you're done.

    docker compose down

    Downloaded models stay in the ollama_data volume, so the next docker compose up -d starts without re-downloading.

  2. Optional: remove the downloaded models too.

    docker compose down -v
path: How to run a local coding agent with Ollama in Docker

items.title: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Using the Ollama CLI from the terminal is the quickest way to chat with a local model. Open WebUI adds a browser-based chat interface on top of your local Ollama instance.

This guide is useful if you want to:

  • use a local model but aren't comfortable with the terminal
  • switch between models without typing commands
  • upload documents and chat with them locally
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
If you haven't run a local model yet, start with How to run a local model with Ollama.

Python version

Open WebUI requires Python 3.11 or 3.12 to be installed to avoid compatibility issues. Refer to Open WebUI documentation for supported versions.

Ollama must be running before you start Open WebUI. If you installed Ollama using the previous guide it runs automatically in the background. You can confirm it is running by visiting http://localhost:11434 in your browser - you should see Ollama is running.
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: Install and run Open WebUI
items.text:
1. Install Open WebUI with pip. We recommend doing this inside a virtual environment to keep its dependencies separate from other projects.
pip install open-webui
  1. Start Open WebUI.
open-webui serve
  1. Open http://localhost:8080 in your browser.
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: Set up your account
items.text:
1. Create an admin account on first launch. This account is local; no data leaves your machine.

  2. Open WebUI will detect Ollama automatically. You should see your downloaded models available in the model selector at the top of the chat window.

  3. Select a model and send a message to confirm everything is working.
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: Troubleshooting
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: No models appear in the selector
items.text: You need to have pulled at least one model with Ollama before Open WebUI can list them. Run ollama pull qwen3.5:2b in your terminal, then refresh the browser.
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: Port is already in use
items.text:
Start Open WebUI on another available port, such as 3001:

open-webui serve --port 3001

Then open http://localhost:3001 in your browser.
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: Stop and clean up
items.text: To stop Open WebUI when you are done: Press Ctrl+C in the terminal where Open WebUI is running.
path: How to add a browser chat to Ollama with Open WebUI

items.title: How to run a local model with Ollama
path: How to run a local model with Ollama

items.title: Overview
items.text:
This guide explains how to run a small local model using Ollama's CLI. It is a good starting point for anyone looking to run a local model.

The guide works for any local system since it does not require a GPU and runs on any operating system (Windows, macOS, Linux).
path: How to run a local model with Ollama

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
This guide assumes you have a basic understanding of the terminal.

We recommend starting with a Qwen3.5 model. Select the specific model based on the available RAM on your local system:

  • Qwen3.5:2B for less than 16GB of RAM
  • Qwen3.5:4B for 16GB+ of RAM
path: How to run a local model with Ollama

items.title: Run the Qwen3.5 model
items.text:
1. Install Ollama.

    Use Ollama's installation instructions for your operating system.

  2. Run the Ollama CLI from the terminal. Type ollama run qwen3.5:2b in the terminal. This command will download the model and run it in ollama.

    ollama run qwen3.5:2b

    You should see a list of available commands.

    ❯ ollama
Ollama 0.32.5

▸ Chat, Code, & Work
    Chat with models, code, search the web, and delegate real work

  Launch Claude Code
    Anthropic's coding tool with subagents

  Launch OpenCode
    Anomaly's open-source coding agent

  Launch Hermes Agent (install)
    Self-improving AI agent built by Nous Research

  Launch OpenClaw (install)
    Personal AI with 100+ skills


↑/↓ navigate • enter launch • → configure • esc quit

  3. Select "Chat, Code, & Work" to launch the chat interface.

    You will see this output:

    ❯ ollama
Select model to run: Type to filter...

  Recommended
  ▸ glm-5.2:cloud (Sign in required)
      Long-horizon coding and agentic engineering with a solid 1M context
    minimax-m3:cloud
      State-of-the-art coding & agent capabilities with multimodal reasoning and
    gemma4:26b
      Agentic workflows and multimodal reasoning, ~19GB, (not downloaded)

  More
    gemma4:12b
    qwen3.5:2b

↑/↓ navigate • enter select • ← back

  4. Type qwen3.5:2b to use the Qwen3.5:2B model.

    You will see this output:

    ❯ ollama
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ what changed on this branch?                                                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
  qwen3.5:2b

  5. Enter a prompt in the text box.

    ❯ ollama
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ What standard library in Python is used to run asynchronous code             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
  qwen3.5:2b

  6. View the model's response.

    Congratulations! You have successfully run a small model locally on your machine.

  7. Optional: Type another prompt.

  8. Enter /bye to exit the prompt and then ESC to quit Ollama.
path: How to run a local model with Ollama

items.title: A vision of the Satyrn ecosystem
path: A vision of the Satyrn ecosystem

items.title: Satyrn's Core
items.text:
Our initial focus

  1. Humans who want trusted and transparent AI Models and tools
  2. High quality learning materials that help the community learn, create, and share ideas and expertise
  3. serve beginners and experts and everyone in between
  4. be concrete in our language and terms; reduce jargon so it is not a barrier
  5. Technical projects
  6. A fully open, local model
  7. Tools that work from terminal, web (notebooks), and as local applications
  8. Tools that leverage Python's techincal strengths
path: A vision of the Satyrn ecosystem

items.title: Satyrn Inner Ring 1 - Open Python Tools and Libraries
items.text: Share knowledge about open source Python Tools and packages from across the ecosystem that serve our mission.
path: A vision of the Satyrn ecosystem

items.title: Satyrn Inner Ring 2 - Domain specific tools and libraries
items.text: Here our focus is on specific domains and how they use Satyrn's tools and philosophy - Medical - Community advocacy - Climate research - Education - and more
path: A vision of the Satyrn ecosystem

items.title: Satyrn in the Universe
items.text:
We recognize that "one-size does not fit all".

The universe contains models and tools that are closed or not fully open, languages other than Python. We try to clarify what other constellations (tools) in the universe offer, their benefits, their limitations, and their use cases.

Python's 30+ years of success was consistent focus on the education and growth of the community. Education is a Python superpower on par with the language.
path: A vision of the Satyrn ecosystem

items.title: What drove Jupyter's success
items.text:
• Fully open source code
  • Open collaboration with a minimum of private meetings/repos
  • Composable and extensible architecture to meet diverse use cases and scientific domains
  • Users able to get work done easily; minimal learning curve to using notebook
  • The ability to combine prose, code, viz, audio/video, and interactivity into one document
  • A Gallery of Interesting Notebooks, curated by the community, that demonstrated the domains served and capabilities of the notebook
  • Initial focus was to serve scientific computing and education; data science came in the second wave
  • The ability for the notebook to serve as a vehicle for sharing knowledge

items.title: Some Jupyter Architecture Goals
items.text:
• Meet people where they work
    • Terminal
    • Web
    • Local application
    • Sharing documents on web
  • Focused on the core and trusted the community to extend where we didn't have knowledge or capacity
  • Used the strengths of Python and JS working together
  • Emphasis on "Don't Make Me Think" design in libraries, projects, and documentation
  • A shareable artifact with a defined spec (.ipynb file)

items.title: Gallery of Interesting Notebooks
items.text: The early days, this wiki page on GitHub was incredibly valuable. Curated by the community and the Project, it shared the variety of domains that Notebooks were useful (sciences, social sciences, and humanities). It also shared creative uses of the notebook and its interactive widgets.

items.title: Glossary
items.text:
A glossary of common terms using throughout this project.

Agent

A system where an AI model is given tools, memory, or the ability to take actions, and operates with some degree of autonomy to complete a goal.

Deep learning

A subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers to approach complex tasks.

Guardrail

A constraint applied to a model's behaviour to prevent unwanted outputs (e.g. harmful content, going off-topic, hallucinating facts).

LLM - Large Language Model

A type of AI model trained on large amounts of text data that can generate, summarise, and reason about language.

Local model

An AI system run on your own machine rather than accessed via the cloud.

Machine learning

A subset of AI where systems learn patterns from data rather than following explicitly programmed rules. Deep learning and LLMs fall within this category.

Prompt

The input given to an AI that tells it what to do.

SDD - Spec-Driven Development

A software development methodology where behaviour is defined in a formal specification document first, and code is then generated and validated against that spec.

Token

The unit a language model processes text in. Models have a context window measured in tokens.

Note

If you would like to add a term to the glossary, please file an issue or open a pull request on GitHub.

Please open an issue or PR to add a site to this guide.

items.title: Sites
items.text:

Materials on this site are not peer-reviewed by arXiv.
